project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer:
Lab-validated devices built on new advanced materials that markedly improve electricity generation, storage or transmission, designed for future grid integration.
This is a Challenge (a themed topic with its own objectives) of the EIC Pathfinder, the European Innovation Council's scheme for early-stage research towards breakthrough technologies. Each project must "identify, develop and validate in the lab, devices based on cutting-edge novel advanced materials" (materials, including nanomaterials, engineered to have properties superior to conventional ones), focusing on one of three areas of the electricity system.

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer:
Each project must pick one of three areas, generation, storage or transmission grids, and develop lab-validated material-based devices meant for grid integration.
Mandatory:
- Address one of the three pillars: energy generators with much higher efficiency, durability and cost-effectiveness and less use of critical raw materials (CRMs, scarce materials the EU depends on importing); storage systems with sharply higher energy density, life cycle, safety and sustainability, focused on helping future grids with high renewable shares handle stability, reliability and resilience; or next-generation transmission grids with much higher efficiency that dramatically reduce losses, improve capacity and enhance grid resilience.
- Design the innovation for practical use in devices or systems intended for grid integration.
- Develop a mid- to long-term roadmap on how and when the innovation will integrate into electrical grids and what measurable advantages it brings over existing solutions.
- Take part in joint portfolio activities with the other selected projects.
Optional: AI methods to speed up materials development, ideally using European AI engines with data stored in Europe.
Limits: the selection funds no more than 3 projects per pillar. All EIC Pathfinder work is for civil applications only.

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer:
Lab-validated devices, a grid-integration roadmap, publications, protected intellectual property and an assessment of regulation and standards.
- Devices based on new advanced materials, validated in the lab and showing significantly enhanced performance in the chosen pillar
- A mid- to long-term roadmap for integration into electrical grids, with the specific, measurable advantages over existing solutions
- Top-level scientific publications
- Adequate formal protection of the intellectual property generated
- An assessment of relevant regulation, certification and standardisation aspects
- Contributions to the portfolio's comparative assessment of devices and systems and their maturity for grid integration

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer:
The result is a lab-validated device, not a product; the project must show a credible route to grid integration and protect and exploit its results.
- Wider use: no replication or deployment is required during the project; the roadmap must show how and when the innovation would integrate into grids and its measurable advantages.
- Standards: the project must assess regulation, certification and standardisation, and for up to 4 years after the project must tell the EU agency if results could contribute to European or international standards.
- Exploitation: beneficiaries must use their best efforts to exploit results, preferably through organisations in Member States or Associated Countries; the agency may object to a transfer of ownership or an exclusive licence, and exploitation must be reported on request for 4 years after the final payment.
- Sharing: the EIC Programme Manager may ask for information on results, which is shared in confidence with other EIC projects.
- Follow-on: projects may receive Booster grants of up to EUR 50,000, apply to EIC Transition (the next EIC scheme, towards market) and, for SMEs, to the EIC Accelerator through the Fast Track scheme.

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer:
One organisation alone, two partners, or three or more partners may apply; the call sets no maximum.
- One organisation (a single beneficiary, the organisation that signs the grant agreement and receives the grant): it must be established in an EU Member State or an Associated Country (a non-EU country that takes part in Horizon Europe on near-equal terms).
- Two partners: two independent organisations from two different Member States or Associated Countries.
- Three or more partners: at least three independent organisations, each in a different country, with at least one in an EU Member State and at least two others in different Member States or Associated Countries.
Affiliated entities (organisations legally linked to a partner that do the work alongside it without signing the grant agreement) do not count towards these minimums.

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer:
No partner type is mandatory, but large companies and mid-caps may not apply alone.
The call names universities, research organisations, SMEs (small and medium-sized enterprises), start-ups and natural persons as examples of eligible organisations. It states: "In the case of single beneficiary projects, mid-caps and larger companies will not be permitted." In a consortium of two or more, the general rules let any legal entity take part, so a large company such as TenneT TSO B.V. may be a partner.
Country rules are those in the partner-number rules (Member States and Associated Countries). Organisations established in China cannot take part in Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Actions in any role.
The call encourages teams to include future leaders such as excellent early-career researchers and promising high-tech SMEs and start-ups, and to empower female researchers.

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer:
No fixed split of work or budget, but a portfolio work package of at least 10 person-months is advised.
Portfolio activities are the joint work with the other projects selected under the same Challenge, steered by the EIC Programme Manager (an EIC official who manages the group of projects). Evaluators score how appropriately person-months and other costs are allocated to work packages and consortium members. Gender balance among work package leaders is encouraged.

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer:
Any eligible partner may lead a consortium; a single-organisation project cannot be led by a large company.
In a consortium the coordinator submits the proposal on behalf of all partners and confirms it has their mandate. The call does not reserve the coordinator role for a particular type of organisation.

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer:
Yes, TenneT TSO B.V. may coordinate a consortium of two or more partners, but it may not apply alone.
The Netherlands is an EU Member State, so TenneT can be the Member State partner a consortium of three must include. A consortium of two needs one partner from another Member State or Associated Country; a consortium of three or more needs at least two further partners, each from a different country. Single-organisation projects exclude large companies. As coordinator TenneT would submit the proposal, prepare the lump-sum budget table with the partners and later lead the joint portfolio work with the EIC Programme Manager. Given the research focus (starting around TRL 2, an early research stage), a university or research organisation would usually lead, but the rules do not require it.

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer:
Yes, either as a funded partner or as an associated partner that receives no money.
The general conditions allow associated partners: organisations that take part in the project without signing the grant agreement and without the right to charge costs. An associated partner does not count towards the minimum number of partners. TenneT could therefore, for example, advise on grid requirements without being a beneficiary.
cards.sources: EIC-2027-Work-Programme.pdf · p. 172 · Annex 2, B.1, Associated partners

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer:
Yes, at 100% of eligible costs, paid as a lump sum, with no lower rate for large companies.
- Funding rate: the grant is a Research and Innovation Action (an EU grant type for research projects) at 100% of eligible costs for every beneficiary, so TenneT would not need to finance part of its own costs.
- Form: a lump sum (a fixed amount agreed during evaluation and paid against completed work rather than against actual costs). The applicants propose it from their estimated costs, which must follow normal EU cost rules.
- Ceiling: up to EUR 4 million per project, shared by all partners, is considered appropriate; more may be requested if duly justified. TenneT's share would therefore come out of that project total.
- Dutch rules: the call sets none; the grant comes directly from the EU through its executive agency (EISMEA).

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer:
The project must produce genuinely new knowledge and technology: new materials and phenomena that go beyond the state of the art.
The call asks for "cutting-edge novel advanced materials" with properties superior to conventional materials and for exploring novel phenomena. Novelty, meaning how far the work goes beyond the state of the art, is part of the Excellence criterion. Integrating existing solutions alone would not meet this.

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer:
The innovation must be in technology: materials and the devices built from them, with a roadmap for integration into grid systems.
The call does not fund market arrangements, governance or operating methods. System aspects enter through the grid-integration roadmap and the portfolio's search for synergies across generation, storage and transmission.

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer:
Research up to lab validation: identifying, developing and validating material-based devices in the lab.
Prototyping for the field, demonstration and deployment are outside the expected path; the roadmap only plans later integration.

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer:
From an early research stage, typically TRL 2, to proof of concept or lab validation at TRL 3 or 4.
TRL is the technology readiness level, a 1–9 scale of how close a technology is to real use: TRL 2 is a formulated technology concept, TRL 4 a technology validated in the lab.

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer:
In the lab only; no demonstration in a real grid or under operating conditions is required.
Devices must be validated in the lab, though designed for later practical use in grid-connected devices or systems.
cards.sources: EIC-2027-Work-Programme.pdf · pp. 41–43 · II.2.1 Breakthroughs in Advanced Materials for Electricity Generation, Storage and Transmission, Specific Objectives

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer:
Each project must design its device for grid integration, and the selected projects must work together as a portfolio.
- Link to existing infrastructure: through the roadmap on how and when the device would integrate into electrical grids.
- Portfolio: projects are selected partly on expected synergies across generation, storage and transmission that could lead to integrated solutions; they must cooperate with each other under the EIC Programme Manager and contribute to a common Challenge roadmap.

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer:
Lab results must show significantly enhanced device performance and measurable advantages over existing solutions; the call sets no numeric indicators.
The performance dimensions differ per area:
- Generation: efficiency, durability, cost-effectiveness, reduced use of critical raw materials
- Storage: energy density, life cycle, safety, sustainability
- Transmission: efficiency, energy losses, capacity, grid resilience
The portfolio will compare the devices and their maturity for grid integration.

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer:
The call does not require users to take part, but the grid-integration roadmap gives grid operators a natural role in setting requirements.
The general Pathfinder text encourages involving future leaders such as high-tech SMEs and start-ups; user co-design or validation is not mandated.

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer:
Safety is a required performance dimension for storage devices; otherwise the general ethics and security rules apply.
- Storage projects must show a sharp increase in safety among other properties.
- AI used for materials development should ideally rely on European AI engines with data stored in Europe (an encouragement, not a rule).
- An ethics self-assessment is required; classified or sensitive information triggers a security appraisal.

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
Up to EUR 4 million of EU contribution per project, from EUR 82 million shared across three Challenges.
- Total project size: the call sets no limit on total project costs; at a 100% rate the grant can cover all estimated eligible costs.
- Grant request: up to EUR 4 million per project (for all partners together); larger amounts are possible if duly justified. With roughly equal shares, each Challenge has about EUR 27 million (an estimate from the stated budget).
- Funding form: lump sum (a fixed amount agreed during evaluation and paid against completed work, not against actual costs).

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
One rate for all: 100% of eligible costs for every beneficiary, including large companies, with no own contribution required.
- Co-financing conditions: none; the call requires no cash or in-kind contribution from partners.

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
A lump sum built on a detailed budget table that follows normal EU cost rules; ineligible costs can reduce the grant.
- Eligible costs: personnel, subcontracting, purchases (equipment, goods, services) and, where used, unit costs; the personnel costs of researchers in the EIC Next Generation Innovation Talents scheme are eligible.
- Caps or mandatory allocations: at least 10 person-months are advised for a work package on portfolio activities.
- Overheads and VAT: indirect costs are a 25% flat rate on direct costs, excluding subcontracting and some other categories.
- Subcontracting or equipment: purchases and subcontracting must give best value for money and be free of conflicts of interest.

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
An advance at the start, minus 5–8% for an EU insurance fund; overpayments are repaid at the end.
- Payment model: pre-financing (an advance) of normally 160% of the average EU funding per reporting period, then interim payments linked to periodic reports and a final payment.
- Retention or guarantee: 5% to 8% of the maximum grant is deducted from the pre-financing and paid into the mutual insurance mechanism (a fund that covers money the EU cannot recover from beneficiaries).
- Financial reporting or audit: a certificate on the financial statements may be required, depending on grant size and beneficiary type. Each beneficiary is liable only for its own debts.

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: a full proposal on the Funding & Tenders Portal (the EU's online application system) by 29 September 2027, 17:00 Brussels time.
- Stage 1 — Full proposal: 29 September 2027, 17:00 Brussels time; Part B sections 1–3 (Excellence, Impact, Implementation) at most 30 A4 pages; open to all eligible applicants. The call opens on 27 May 2027; the opening may move by up to one month and the deadline may be delayed by up to two months.
- Additional procedure: none; there is no interview for the Pathfinder Challenges.
cards.sources: EIC-2027-Work-Programme.pdf · p. 37 · II.2, How do you apply; how long does it take? and footnote 47

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The call sets no duration or start date; both are fixed in the grant agreement.
- Required start: normally after the grant agreement is signed; an earlier start can be granted only exceptionally and for duly justified reasons.
cards.sources: EIC-2027-Work-Programme.pdf · p. 194 · Annex 2, G.1 Starting date and project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
Results are expected about 5 months after the deadline and grant agreements about 8 months after it, both indicative.
- Expected assessment result: by about the end of February 2028 (5 months after the deadline, indicative).
- Grant agreement: signed by about the end of May 2028 (8 months after the deadline, indicative); after the letter announcing selection, preparation and signature is expected within three months.
- Conditions before starting: legal entity validation of each partner's PIC (participant identification code), financial capacity and exclusion checks, any ethics review, and a consortium agreement that settles ownership of results and dissemination approvals. The EIC Project Officer and Programme Manager help plan the portfolio activities during grant preparation.

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
A two-part online application with a detailed lump-sum budget table and an ethics self-assessment; incomplete applications are ineligible.
- Application form: Part A (administrative data, filled in online) and Part B (technical description, uploaded as PDF), using the forms in the Portal submission system; Part B sections 1–3 at most 30 A4 pages.
- Budget: a detailed budget table that justifies the proposed lump sum.
- Mandatory annexes: the ethics self-assessment, and a plan for exploitation and dissemination of results including communication activities.
- Partner documents: the coordinator confirms it has the mandate of all applicants; each partner signs a declaration of honour before the grant.
- Registration: every beneficiary and affiliated entity must register in the Participant Register to get a PIC before submitting.

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Proposals are scored against three criteria with thresholds, then a committee picks a balanced portfolio rather than simply the top scores.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence (objectives and relevance to the Challenge, novelty, plausibility of the methodology); Impact (credible pathways to the Challenge outcomes, innovation potential, communication and dissemination); Quality and efficiency of the implementation (work plan, allocation of resources, quality of the applicant or consortium).
- Thresholds: Excellence 4 out of 5; Impact 4 out of 5; Implementation 3 out of 5.
- Weighting: Excellence 50%, Impact 30%, Implementation 20%.
- Ranking rules: all proposals above the thresholds go to a second step, where an evaluation committee of experts and EIC Programme Managers maps them into categories and selects a coherent portfolio of projects; it may propose minor adjustments.
- Budget assessment: the lump sum is fixed during evaluation and can be lower than requested; budget comments are given for proposals invited, reserved, or rejected for clearly over- or underestimated costs.

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Telecom-network elements, ethics issues and classified information trigger extra checks; reading the Challenge Guide is strongly encouraged.
- Conditional — elements on European communication networks (5G and later): the proposal is subject to restrictions to protect those networks.
- Conditional — ethics issues: an ethics review before funding, with possible ethics deliverables in the grant agreement.
- Conditional — classified or sensitive information: a security appraisal before funding and specific security rules.
- Recommended — read the Challenge Guide (a document with the Challenge's technical background and portfolio considerations), which the EIC will publish on its website and the Funding & Tenders Portal.
- Recommended — involve early-career researchers and high-tech SMEs or start-ups, and aim for gender balance among work package leaders.
